description: Send events at given times without rendering anything, and get active states and property values over time, plus a per-property summary: min, max, final value, and when it came to rest.

events.description: What happens, in time order. Each item is an event { "event": "track.tap", "t": 0.1 }, an input sample { "input": "track.drag.x", "value": 12, "t": 0.2 }, or a whole drag { "drag": "track", "t": 0.1, "until": 0.3, "dx": 20 } (down, dragstart, 60 samples per second, up, dragend).

dx.description: Horizontal travel of the drag, in logical units.

dy.description: Vertical travel of the drag, in logical units.

t.description: Seconds, or a string like "100ms". For a drag, when it starts.

file.description: Path to a .nudg.json file, relative to the working directory.

layout.description: What the host would measure (0.4), reported at time 0: { "tab2.x": 96, "tab2.width": 88, "underline.x": 8 }. Measured values without it fall back to their base.

path.description: With `source`: where the text would live, for resolving imports and labeling.

properties.description: Properties to report, e.g. ["knob.x"]. Default: all.

reducedMotion.description: Play as a reduced-motion user would see it: short linear tweens, no kicks (0.3).

rev.description: With `file`: read it as it was at this git revision (HEAD, HEAD~1, a branch) instead of from disk, imports included.

source.description: The file's JSON text, to check before writing it. Imports resolve relative to `path`, or the working directory.

start.description: Start in these states instead of initial, e.g. ["on"].

until.description: Last time to look at. Default: when everything has come to rest.

name: nudg_simulate
title: Simulate a nudg file
